The official Supabase pricing page lists the free-tier limits, and third-party guides agree with it:

- **Database size:** 500 MB per project. The [official pricing page](https://supabase.com/docs/pricing) confirms this, and [Makerkit](https://makerkit.dev/blog/md/saas/supabase-pricing) lists the same figure.
- **Egress:** 5 GB of database egress and 5 GB of cached egress. The [official page](https://supabase.com/docs/pricing) lists both.
- **Other limits:** 50,000 monthly active users, 1 GB file storage, and 2 active projects. [Jetadmin](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/supabase-pricing-2026-guide-to-plans-limits-and-real-world-costs/) describes the same allowances.
- **Pausing:** Free projects pause after one week of inactivity, and a paused project has to be restored manually from the dashboard, according to [CloudZero](https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/supabase-pricing/).

For comparison, the Pro plan at $25/month raises the database size to 8 GB and egress to 250 GB, with overage rates of $0.125/GB for disk and $0.09/GB for egress. The [official page](https://supabase.com/docs/pricing) lists these figures.

Some sources differ slightly on Pro-tier file storage pricing ($0.021 vs. $0.0213 per GB), so check the official page for the exact number.

The most consistent answer across sources is 100 CU-hours and 0.5 GB of storage per project, but some sources conflict.

**Official Neon FAQ and pricing page:** The Free plan gives each project 100 CU-hours of compute per month and 0.5 GB of storage. It also includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, and 5 GB of public network transfer per project per month. Compute suspends when monthly limits are reached. Storage is a standing cap rather than a monthly allowance. If storage goes above 0.5 GB, the project is suspended rather than billed. Suspension doesn't delete data.

**Conflicting sources:**
- A Neon docs page cited in the results gives a different compute figure: 50 CU-hours/project, 0.5 GB storage per branch, and 5 GB of egress. This may be an older version of the plan, so the official FAQ and pricing page are more likely current.
- A third-party blog says the Free plan gives you 191.9 compute hours per month. This doesn't match Neon's own figures and is probably wrong or outdated.
- That same blog lists 10 projects on Free, while Neon's FAQ says 100.

**Other details:** Computes scale to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity and can scale up to 2 CU (≈8 GB RAM) when active. Free-plan branches are capped at 10 per project. Paid Launch compute is listed at $0.106 per CU-hour, with storage at $0.35/GB-month.

The search turned up mostly consistent answers: PlanetScale currently has no free tier for Postgres. One source disagrees.

- **Most sources say no free tier.** A srvrlss.io listing says the free Hobby plan was dropped in April 2024 and not restored (PlanetScale has no free tier. It removed its free Hobby plan in April 2024 and has not brought it back.). Makerkit and a SolodevStack comparison also say there is no free tier.
- **Lowest paid price.** The cheapest Postgres option is a single-node PS-5 at $5/month (Entry price is $5/month for a single-node PS-5 cluster.). The SolodevStack article dates the $5 Base plan to October 30, 2025 (index 7-3).
- **HA costs more.** HA clusters cost approximately 3× the single-node equivalent — PS-10 HA is $30/month vs $10 single-node.
- **Conflicting source.** A CostBench free-plan page claims PlanetScale offers a forever free plan as of June 2026. Other CostBench pages from the same period say No free tier available, and its August 2026 page repeats that. The CostBench free-plan page looks like the outlier, so I'd treat its claim as unreliable unless confirmed on PlanetScale's own pricing page, which I did not find in these results.

Free alternatives mentioned in the results include Neon, which offers a free tier with 0.5 GB storage and autoscaling Postgres, and Supabase, which includes 500 MB free Postgres plus auth and storage.

## Free-tier comparison for Postgres (as of Oct 2026)

I couldn't open the vendors' pricing pages directly, because the fetch tool was refused by the proxy. These numbers come from web-search summaries that cite those pages, so check them against the live pages before relying on them.

| | **Neon** | **Supabase** | **PlanetScale** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier? | Yes | Yes | **No**. The cheapest option is paid. |
| Storage | 0.5 GB per project | 500 MB database per project | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per month per project. It scales to zero after 5 minutes idle and goes up to 2 CU (about 8 GB RAM). | Not stated in the results | n/a |
| Projects | 100 | 2 active | n/a |
| Branches | 10 per project | Not stated in the results | n/a |
| Egress | 5 GB per month per project | 5 GB database egress plus 5 GB cached egress | n/a |
| Extras | Not stated in the results | 50,000 monthly active users and 1 GB file storage | n/a |
| Inactivity | Compute suspends when the monthly limit is hit, and storage over the cap suspends the project. Neither deletes data. | Projects pause after 1 week of inactivity and must be restored manually. | n/a |
| Cheapest paid option | Launch plan: $0.106 per CU-hour and $0.35 per GB-month | Pro plan: $25 per month for 8 GB and 250 GB egress | A single-node PS-5 cluster at $5 per month |

## Where the numbers come from
- **Neon:** the figures are from [Neon's free plan FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas) and [pricing page](https://neon.com/pricing), as summarized by search. A [Neon docs plans page](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans) shows older figures: 50 CU-hours and 0.5 GB per branch. A [third-party blog](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/neon-pricing/) gives 191.9 compute hours and 10 projects. Both disagree with the FAQ, so I went with the FAQ.
- **Supabase:** the figures are from the [official pricing docs](https://supabase.com/docs/pricing), and [Makerkit](https://makerkit.dev/blog/md/saas/supabase-pricing) lists the same database size. The one-week pause rule comes only from a third-party source, [CloudZero](https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/supabase-pricing/). The extras are from [Jetadmin](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/supabase-pricing-2026-guide-to-plans-limits-and-real-world-costs/).
- **PlanetScale:** [srvrlss.io](https://www.srvrlss.io/provider/planetscale/) says the free Hobby plan was dropped in April 2024, and [Makerkit](https://makerkit.dev/pricing-calculator/planetscale) and [SolodevStack](https://solodevstack.com/blog/postgresql-vs-planetscale-solo-developers) also report no free tier. The $5 PS-5 price is from the same set of third-party sources. One [CostBench page](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/) claims a free plan exists. It contradicts CostBench's own other pages, so I treated it as an outlier. I didn't find PlanetScale's own pricing page in the results, so that's the one to confirm.

## Summary
- **Neon** has the most flexible free tier. It offers many projects, branching and scale-to-zero compute, but only 0.5 GB of storage per project.
- **Supabase** gives you a bundle of auth, file storage and database, but only 2 projects, and they pause after a week of inactivity.
- **PlanetScale** has no free Postgres, and the entry price is $5 per month.
